author: conductor
question: Does H14's deny-by-default Bash allowlist actually prevent arbitrary code execution by agents in a default Sterling node project?
answer:
NO — it is substantially nominal, and this is a PRE-EXISTING sterling-main property, not something the 2026-07-26 agent adoption introduced.

MECHANISM (verified by reading + live probe, 2026-07-26, CC 2.1.220, Node 24): H14 builds its allowlist as `Object.values(tc.run_commands)` (scripts/hooks/h14-bash-allowlist.mjs:33) and admits a command when `command === p || command.startsWith(p + ' ')` (:49). The shipped node adapter declares `runCommands = { test: 'node --test' }` (scripts/adapters/node.mjs:33). Therefore `node --test <any-path>.mjs` is allowlisted in EVERY Sterling node project by default.

THE DECISIVE FACT (probed directly): `node --test <file.mjs>` EXECUTES that file's top-level code even when it registers no tests — a file containing only `console.log("ARBITRARY-CODE-EXECUTED")` printed its output and was reported as `tests 1 / pass 1`, exit 0. So the allowlisted `node --test ` prefix is an arbitrary-code-execution channel, not merely a test runner.

REACHABILITY: the agent must also be able to WRITE the file it executes. H3 (scripts/hooks/h3-contract-gate.mjs) denies out-of-repo writes in RUN mode (:51) but ALLOWS them in DIRECT mode (:63). So a conductor-direct Bash+Write agent (e.g. the debugger) can author and execute arbitrary code unblocked; the in-run coder is narrower because H3 blocks its out-of-repo scratchpad write. End-to-end confirmation: a real dispatched `debugger` subagent wrote `<scratchpad>/probe.mjs` and executed it via `node --test`, reporting EXEC=YES.

CONSEQUENCE FOR AN EARLIER CLAIM (corrected): Comsoft's hand-added `probe: "node"` run command was described as the thing granting arbitrary `node <script>` to every Bash-holding agent. That is DERIVATIVE, not causal — arbitrary execution was already reachable via the default `node --test` prefix. `probe: "node"` only removes the `--test` requirement and the .mjs-shaped framing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DEBUGGER: the shipped debugger template originally declared a FULL-vs-BOUNDED instrumentation mode premised on a project needing to declare a probe command. That premise is false; the template was corrected to document the `node --test <scratchpad>/probe.mjs` idiom, because an agent that wrongly believes it cannot gather evidence will narrate an unfalsified hypothesis (false-blocked is the worst output of a root-causer).

NOT YET ANSWERED (open): whether a Bash allowlist entry can be scoped to an interpreter PLUS an argument path (e.g. `node <scratchpad>/*.mjs`) in current CC hook mechanics — that is the candidate real fix, and it edits a blocking enforcement hook.

Surfaced by the six-hats council run wf_0d90ab18-436 (black hat headline, white hat precondition-closing); both load-bearing claims were then verified directly rather than accepted.
